compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`ready_tickets` is bounded at 90,000 bytes by bug `daughterly-agitative-ocelot`
(`494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0`), but even after that fix's lean projection it sits at **58 rows /
87,893 wire bytes — roughly ONE row of headroom**. The bound is correct and its refusal is
actionable (it points at `next_batch`), but the tool will begin refusing its default call
about as soon as one more ticket becomes ready. That is a cliff, not a fixed problem.

## The question this ticket answers

Does a DISCOVERY surface need near-full ticket rows at all? `ready_tickets` answers "what can
I work on next". Measured on the real store (58 ready rows, 90,000-byte budget):

| shape | bytes/row | rows that fit | headroom vs today |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| as shipped (lean, `TicketStateOut`) | 1,515 | 59 | +1 |
| lean minus `file_impact`/`deps`/author/env fields | 801 | 112 | +54 |
| summary fields, still via `TicketStateOut` | 572 | 157 | +99 |
| summary fields via a NEW closed output model | 234 | 384 | +326 |

Two findings drive this:

1. **The lean ready row still carries fields a discovery caller cannot use.** `file_impact` is
   252 B/row (18.1% of the row) and `deps` 160 B/row (11.5%) — 30% of the payload between them,
   for a question that only needs id/alias/title/type/status/priority and blocking state.
2. **`TicketStateOut`'s declared defaults set a floor.** Projecting to summary fields but
   returning `TicketStateOut` still costs 572 B/row, because `model_validate` re-adds
   `description: null`, `comments: []`, `deps: []`, `inbound_deps: []`, `file_impact: []`,
   `file_impact_scope`, `no_file_impact_reason`, `plan_review_health: null` and
   `cross_session_warning: null`. **338 of those 572 bytes are re-added defaults** — the same
   mechanism that made the parent bug's budget under-estimate by 178%. Reaching 234 B/row
   requires a different, closed output model, which changes the tool's `outputSchema`.

## Scope decision this ticket must make

The cheap half (row 2 of the table) is a further narrowing along the axis
`494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0` ALREADY declared breaking, so it folds into that existing release note
and needs no schema change. The large half (row 4) changes the declared `outputSchema` and
interacts with `full=True`, which must still return the whole shape — so the tool would carry
two result types. `docs/api-stability.md` treats declared output schemas as a strong contract,
so that half deserves its own decision rather than riding along.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether `ready_tickets` returns a discovery-shaped result via a
      new closed output model, or is merely narrowed further within `TicketStateOut`, with the
      `full=True` behaviour stated for whichever is chosen.
- [ ] Default `ready_tickets` has headroom for at least 3x the current ready count on this
      store, measured on the wire payload (post-`model_validate`, post-`js_safe_result`), not on
      raw reducer rows.
- [ ] Any further narrowing of a default output is recorded in `docs/release-notes.md` and
      `CHANGELOG.md` — folded into the existing `494b` entry if it is the same axis, or as its
      own entry if the declared `outputSchema` changes.
- [ ] `list_tickets` is explicitly considered and the asymmetry justified in the change: it has
      six filter arguments, so an over-budget refusal there is actionable and the budget is a
      guardrail rather than a cliff; `ready_tickets` has none.
- [ ] Regression coverage asserts the per-row size ceiling, so the row cannot silently re-grow.
